title: Draft Professional Writing with AI, Then Take Back the Edit
subtitle: Use AI for a fast first pass; keep intent, facts, tone, and final wording under human control
description: For routine professional writing, give AI the purpose, audience, constraints, and source facts, ask for a draft, then revise it yourself. Controlled evidence supports productivity gains for some professional writing tasks, not automatic accuracy or judgment.

lifeOsSource.hack: Use AI to produce a constrained first draft, then rewrite the parts where facts, intent, tone, or accountability matter.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Provide the audience, goal, source facts, must-include points, and constraints. Ask for one draft. Compare it with the source material, remove invented details, restore your own judgment and voice, and send only the version you can defend without the model in the room.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Did AI reduce drafting time without introducing claims, tone, or commitments I would not have written myself?
lifeOsSource.reference: Noy & Zhang (2023) — Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence

faq.question: Should I send the AI draft as-is?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as draft material. Check facts, names, numbers, commitments, tone, and anything that could matter to another person before sending.

faq.question: What did the experiment actually show?
faq.answer: In one preregistered experiment with mid-level professional writing tasks, participants with ChatGPT completed tasks faster on average and received higher quality ratings. That does not prove the same gain for every writing task, model, or workplace.

intro.html: AI is unusually good at making the blank page less blank. That is useful. It is not the same as being responsible for what the page says.

sections.title: 1. Give it a real brief
sections.html: State the audience, purpose, length, tone, source facts, and any non-negotiable points. A vague prompt mostly asks the model to invent the missing brief for you.

sections.title: 2. Ask for one workable draft
sections.html: Use the first pass to create structure and wording quickly. Do not spend ten rounds polishing a weak premise; fix the premise yourself if the task is underspecified.

sections.title: 3. Reconcile every material claim
sections.html: Check names, dates, numbers, quotations, promises, legal or policy language, and anything presented as fact against the original source. Remove details the model supplied without evidence.

sections.title: 4. Take back the final edit
sections.html: Rewrite the parts that carry your judgment or relationship with the reader. The final test is simple: would you still stand behind the message if nobody knew AI helped draft it?

references.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
references.claim_scope: In a preregistered experiment with 453 college-educated professionals completing mid-level professional writing tasks, access to ChatGPT reduced average completion time and increased average quality ratings. The study does not establish equivalent gains for every writing task or guarantee factual accuracy.

editorialCuration.reason: Publish as a bounded AI writing workflow: evidence supports task-level productivity gains in a specific professional-writing experiment, while the protocol keeps factual verification and final accountability human.
